# Josie Pye

## Overview

- **Status:** alive  _(assumed)_

## Appearance

_Not yet known._

## Personality

Josie Pye is known for her disagreeable demeanor, sharp tongue, and lack of imagination, traits that render her lacking in general popularity. Despite this, she possesses specific talents, such as a cultivated skill for walking board fences and an award-winning ability at knitting lace. Her goal in attending college is simply for the sake of education, as she does not need to earn her own living.

## History

Josie Pye won first prize for knitted lace at the [Exhibition](../codex/places.md#exhibition). She attended [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school alongside her classmates, later becoming part of the social group involved in games, parties, and school activities. When Miss [Stacy](../character/stacy.md) formed an advanced class to prepare students for the [Entrance](../codex/places.md#entrance) examination to Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#academy), Josie was among the pupils selected to undertake the rigorous studies. She ultimately moved to [Charlottetown](../codex/places.md#charlottetown) to attend Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#academy) with her peers, pursuing her education through to Commencement.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P1](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER XV. ## Quotes

> “Oh, that reminds me,” said Josie, “Queen’s is to get one of the Avery scholarships after all. The word came today. Frank Stockley told me—his uncle is one of the board of governors, you know. It will be announced in the Academy tomorrow.”
>
> — Josie Pye — [v1 CHAPTER XXXIV. A Queen’s Girl P24](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0024)

> "If I don’t pass this year I’m coming back next. My father can afford to send me. Anne, Frank Stockley says that Professor Tremaine said Gilbert Blythe was sure to get the medal and that Emily Clay would likely win the Avery scholarship."
>
> — Josie Pye — [v1 CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Queen’s P14](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0014)

> "I dare you to climb up there and walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry’s kitchen roof."
>
> — Josie Pye — [v1 CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor P11](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0011)

> "I don’t believe anybody could walk a ridgepole. You couldn’t, anyhow."
>
> — Josie Pye — [v1 CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor P9](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0009)

> "Are you going to be back next year, Miss Stacy?"
>
> — Josie Pye — [v1 CHAPTER XXX. The Queen’s Class Is Organized P30](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0030)
